key_insight: COSA-GS makes 3D Gaussian Splatting compression more practical by avoiding expensive spatial context modeling and reducing platform-dependent floating-point issues. The result is a simpler, more robust compression pipeline for storing and transmitting 3DGS models.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the high storage cost of 3D Gaussian Splatting and the practical difficulties of existing compression methods, especially complex training/coding from irregular 3D spatial context modeling and entropy-decoding failures caused by floating-point inconsistencies across platforms.
method: Builds context without relying on spatial aggregation over irregular 3D structures, simplifying compression design.
Targets more stable entropy coding by reducing dependence on floating-point context inference that can vary across hardware/software platforms.
Designs COSA-GS as a practical compression framework focused on robustness and deployability rather than only theoretical compression gains.
impact: This matters for AI/ML practitioners because it makes 3DGS models easier to store, share, and deploy in real systems. It also improves reliability across different platforms, which is critical for reproducible compression and decoding workflows.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing original 3DGS vs. compressed COSA-GS flow
Side-by-side comparison of storage size before and after compression
Icon-based illustration of platform consistency/robust entropy decoding
Simple block diagram highlighting context construction without spatial aggregation
paper_title: Towards Practical Compression of 3D Gaussian Splatting
paper_authors: Pengpeng Yu, Yueru Chen, Fei Song, Tai Qin, Qi Zhang
